properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 3:10PM MDT until October 27 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County, West Central Costilla County,
Southeastern Rio Grande County, and Southwestern Alamosa County...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring, especially in areas along
and near the Conejos River and the Rio Grande. Widespread
inundation of agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying
areas persists. Areas of standing or slow moving water will
continue over many roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 259 PM MDT, Flooding was still occurring in the warning area,
especially in low-lying areas.
- Low lying areas in Conejos, Costilla, Rio Grande and Alamosa
counties are impacted, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 9:07AM MDT until October 29 at 4:17AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Purgatoire River Near Las Animas affecting Bent County.

For the Purgatoire River...including Las Animas...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor Flood. Minor agricultural flooding
occurs into low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 8.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 10.2 feet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood
stage tomorrow afternoon to 3.0 feet Saturday evening. It will
rise to 3.1 feet early Sunday morning. It will then fall again
and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.2
feet on 05/31/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
